scholarships.title: TEF Entrepreneurship Programme
scholarships.degree: Not a degree programme (entrepreneurship training and seed funding)

existing.description: The TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Tony Elumelu Foundation's flagship annual programme for African entrepreneurs, combining business management training, mentorship, coaching and a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award. The application is completed on the TEFConnect digital platform and the business assessment test score determines eligibility. Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. This is a business grant and training programme, not a scholarship, so no tuition or living costs are paid.
eligibility: Applications from Africans who are 18 years and above
Applications from applicants who either have a business idea or have a business no older than 5 years
Applications from Africans who reside in Africa and plan to establish their business in Africa
Applications from applicants who have never benefitted from any of our previous programmes
Applications from applicants who have not previously applied in the same application window of the same year
Name and personal details registered on TEFConnect must exactly match the information on the government-issued ID
existing.eligibility_summary: Africans aged 18 and above who reside in Africa, hold a business idea or a business no older than five years, plan to establish the business in Africa, and have never previously received any TEF programme or previously applied in the same application window of the same year.
benefits: Listing of partner banks where participants are advised to open business accounts for easier fund tracking and disbursement
Onboarding into the TEF Alumni network of business leaders
coverage: USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital, paid into the participant's business account
Access to the TEF Business Management Training on TEFConnect
Mentor pairing, with mentors assigned a maximum of three mentees and committing to a minimum of two hours of mentoring per mentee every month
Business plan and financial projection templates
Certificate of Completion and Achievement and onboarding into the TEF Alumni network
requirements: Register on the TEFConnect digital platform and complete the programme application form
Complete all four sections of the application form: personal information; business idea and experience information; business assessment test; declaration
Complete all mandatory fields in the online application form
Upload a valid, clear and accessible government-issued ID showing date of birth and photo
Attach all requested documents and submit the form
After selection, achieve 100% completion of all training modules on TEFConnect
Participate in coaching sessions and engage with assigned mentors
Submit a business plan, financial projection of the business, and a 2-3 minute pitch video
documents: Valid government-issued ID clearly displaying the participant's headshot and full name, matching TEFConnect and the ID (National Driver's Licence, International Passport, or Permanent Voter's Card for Nigerian participants only)
Business Registration Certificate clearly capturing the name of the business
Evidence of tax registration, which must be in the business name
A valid reference letter from the business' bank clearly capturing the participant's name, the name of their business, and the bank details for the business
A duly completed Partner Consent form (only for co-owners of the business)
A valid medical report from a reputable hospital (only for participants living with disabilities)
application_method: Register on TEFConnect at www.TEFConnect.com when the window opens on 1 January
Complete the four sections of the application form and sit the business assessment test
Upload the government-issued ID and high-resolution headshot, making sure personal details match the ID exactly
Submit the form and note the eligibility notification shown on screen and sent by email
If shortlisted, undergo world-check screening and physical verification, then attend the onboarding session
Complete training modules, coaching and mentorship, then submit the business plan, financial projection and pitch video
Upload the business registration, tax, banking and other documents to receive the USD 5,000 seed capital
existing.selection_notes: Independent third-party experts review eligible applications. A minimum score in the business assessment test is required or the applicant is notified as ineligible and encouraged to reapply the following year. Eligible applicants undergo LSEG World-Check global compliance screening and a physical verification exercise by authorised enumerators, which may be in person or virtual. Shortlisting is evaluated on business feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability, and leadership and entrepreneurial skills. In the investment readiness phase an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video and ranks participants for investment readiness. Shortlisted participants are notified of participation on the 22nd of March each year.
existing.best_fit: Africans aged 18 and above who live in Africa, have a business idea or a business no older than five years, plan to build the business in Africa, and have never received a TEF programme award.
existing.notes: The seed capital is non-refundable and is not a scholarship: it does not pay tuition or living costs, and applicants must fund their own living expenses throughout the cycle. The portal is only open for two months a year, 1 January to midnight 1 March; there is no rolling intake, so missing the window means waiting a full year. You cannot have previously benefited from any TEF programme, and you cannot reapply within the same application window of the same year, which the Foundation states explicitly. Programme participants whose documents are found inauthentic, contain discrepancies, or match the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries are immediately disqualified. Seed capital payment requires signing the seed capital undertaking and is processed into the business account you provide.
existing.duration: Annual cohort cycle: application, due diligence, shortlist, training, investment readiness, then seed capital disbursement
existing.application_period: The application window opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March each year, for that year's cohort. The next published window after 2026-10-01 is 1 January 2027 to midnight 1 March 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Every year, the application portal for our flagship TEF Entrepreneurship Programme opens on the 1st of January till midnight on the 1st of March at Midnight, on our digital platform, www.TEFConnect.com.
existing.program_type: Foundation entrepreneurship grant and training programme

existing.funding_period: up to, over the award duration (usually 5 years)
existing.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.
existing.eligibility_summary: Early-career researcher with a passed PhD viva or at least four years' equivalent research experience, no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, at least 80% of research time on the project, based at an eligible administering organisation.
benefits: If, after two or more years from the activation date, your organisation awards you a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract that includes your salary, you can keep the salary element of the award to use towards your remaining research costs
Award holders who need a visa to work in the UK may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa
The award may be held on a part-time basis, with the duration extended to reflect this; the application must still be costed at 1.0 (100%) full-time equivalent
Access to Wellcome's global talent, mentoring and community networks
coverage: Total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire period of the grant, determined by the administering organisation, including basic salary, employer contributions, pension scheme costs, incremental salary progression and locally recognised allowances
Overheads, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit; total overhead cost should not be more than 20% of direct research costs
Overseas allowances and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit
Adjustment support including assistive technology and support staff, which does not count towards the £400,000 limit
Visa and work permit costs for the grantholder, their partner and dependent children, plus Immigration Health Surcharge costs if in the UK six months or more
Relocation allowance of up to £1,000 to cover personal removal costs
Staff salaries up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post
Conference attendance contributions: £2,000 a year for the grantholder and £1,000 each a year for research and technical staff, plus accredited carbon credits to mitigate emissions
Caring responsibility costs at conferences up to £1,000 per person per conference, subject to the stated conditions

Continuing professional development and professional skills training up to £500 a year per person, and research skills training, for staff in posts of 12 months or more working on the grant at 50% FTE or more
Materials and consumables, animals, equipment purchase and maintenance, computer equipment, and access charges for shared equipment, facilities or services
requirements: Submit your application through Wellcome Funding, and only once all required sections and documents are complete
Obtain a sponsor statement from an individual at your administering organisation who holds an established post for the duration of the award
Identify a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship
If requesting overheads, provide a letter from your Finance Director stating how overhead costs were calculated, including confirmation of any externally validated rate and when it was last reviewed
You must check that your type of research project is within what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research before applying
documents: Research proposal and budget costed in the Wellcome Funding system
Sponsor statement from an individual at the administering organisation holding an established post
Finance Director letter on overhead calculation, if overheads are requested
application_method: Check your eligibility using Wellcome's self-assessment tool
Confirm your research fits what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research
Agree your administering organisation and secure a sponsor and a mentor
Prepare the research proposal and budget, costing salaries on your organisation's pay scales
Complete the application in Wellcome Funding and submit
Wait for assessment and decision; applications can be submitted at any time
existing.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.
existing.best_fit: Researchers with a completed PhD (or equivalent) and no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, from any discipline, based at an eligible UK, Republic of Ireland or eligible LMIC organisation, whose work has potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
existing.notes: Location eligibility is changing on 29 October 2026: from that date Wellcome will only accept applications from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia, so an application submitted in October 2026 from a Republic of Ireland or a Latin American organisation would not be accepted under the new rule. You can only hold one of these awards and Wellcome does not offer renewals. No studentships are provided on this award. You cannot apply if you hold or have accepted an equivalent award at this career stage, or if you have an existing tenured salaried post for the duration of the award (unless based in a low- or middle-income country). You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China. Total resubmission of the same project is capped at two times across all Wellcome schemes. Overheads are not paid to UK research organisations that already receive core funding for overheads.
existing.duration: Usually 5 years, but may be less for some disciplines, and may only be longer if held on a part-time basis
existing.application_period: Rolling, applications accepted year-round. Location eligibility changes on 29 October 2026: from that date applications are only accepted from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia. Applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current location eligibility requirements.
existing.deadline_display: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. Apply anytime - Applications are accepted year-round.
